messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — we still need to decide ownership for the 'eviction' / final-fallback signal during canary/A-B rollouts. central coordinator vs local runtime?
ben: My vote was leaning local for speed, but we need a clear bounded contract so it doesn't do weird evictions.
jin: local w/ central override seems pragmatic. local acts fast, central can veto/restore within the grace window.
samira: Agree. Two practical concerns: telemetry fidelity (local often sees host-level noise) and signal synthesis (we need a single truth for whether user-visible SLA is breaking).
ben: For signal synthesis: local should expose raw metrics and a lightweight aggregator that reports a delta summary to central. central runs the final decision logic unless local hits a hard threshold (emergency stop).
maya: Proposal: default delegation = local (fast stop for severe errors), but central has a short reclaim window (30-60s) where it can override and either escalate or roll back automatically. Also central holds a 'safety bond' so tenants can't mute critical alerts.
rolloutbot: deploybot: canary start id=canary/2026-03-21-07:12 (meta: canary_size=5%, region=us-west) :rocket:
jin: We should encode this in the rollout manifest. Example snippet:
```yaml
fallback:
  delegation: local
  local_hard_thresholds:
    error_rate_pct: 10
    p95_latency_ms: 3000
  central_reclaim_window_s: 45
  telemetry_profile: compact_delta
```
ben: Looks good. A few tradeoffs: 1) central decisions are slower (extra hop, potential clock skew), 2) local-only increases blast radius if local logic is buggy.
samira: To mitigate (2) we add configuration validation at rollout time: compare local policy to central guardrails and require approval if divergence > X. Also add a canary-only 'trial' mode where local decisions must be ACKed by central for first N minutes.
maya: Ops playbook note: if central loses connectivity, local still must be able to enforce a critical stop. But we should flip to conservative mode (prefer fallback to safe variant) not aggressive eviction.
ben: Implementation sketch: runtime exposes /v1/decisions endpoint returning {decision, reason, metrics_signature}. Central periodically pulls compact signatures and evaluates. If central disagrees, it issues /v1/override with TTL. Keep overrides idempotent.
jin: We also need deterministic tie-breakers when both local & central trigger near-simultaneously. Suggest lexicographic by source priority + monotonic sequence number.
samira: Observability: surface three signals in Console: local-stop-count, central-overrides, and cohesion_lag_ms (time between local action and central's view). Alerts if cohesion_lag_ms > 2000ms for more than 1 minute.
maya: UX: rollout manifest should show who owns fallback and show a one-click handback to central. PMs want explicit labels: "autodelegate: local" vs "autodelegate: central".
ben: Dev note: avoid pushing large telemetry payloads on warm paths. compact_delta should be max 1KB per minute per canary.
jin: Also need a test harness: simulate central lose + high error + noisy hosts. Add chaos tests that flip central decisions and measure false-positives of local hard thresholds.
samira: Security: central override must be signed (mTLS + signed token) and recorded in audit logs. Don't allow self-approval by project owners for overrides; require cross-team reviewer for rollback.
maya: Action items: 1) draft guardian API spec (who calls what) — @jin, 2) rollout manifest extension PR — @ben, 3) telemetry compact schema — @samira, 4) add chaos case to canary test matrix — @maya.
ben: I'll open the PR for the manifest today.
rolloutbot: rolloutbot: note: canary/2026-03-21 entered 5% steady-state at 07:15
maya: Thanks — will collate notes into an RFC addendum. :memo:
